cases.sentence: Всё тот же счастливый, улыбающийся черкес, с усиками и блестящими глазами, смотревший из-под ___, сидел там, и этот черкес был Соня, и эта Соня была наверное его будущая, счастливая и любящая жена.
cases.explain: «собольего капора» — after the preposition «из-под», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Then it’s all right?” said Nikoláy, again scrutinizing the expression of his sister’s face to see if she was in earnest. Then he jumped down and, his boots scrunching the snow, ran back to his sleigh. The same happy, smiling Circassian, with mustache and beaming eyes looking up from under a sable hood, was still sitting there, and that Circassian was Sónya, and that Sónya was certainly his future happy and loving wife.

cases.sentence: Раздевшись, но не стирая ___, они долго сидели, разговаривая о своем счастьи.
cases.explain: «пробочных усов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: When they reached home and had told their mother how they had spent the evening at the Melyukóvs’, the girls went to their bedroom. When they had undressed, but without washing off the cork mustaches, they sat a long time talking of their happiness. They talked of how they would live when they were married, how their husbands would be friends, and how happy they would be. On Natásha’s table stood two looking glasses which Dunyásha had prepared beforehand.

cases.sentence: На ___ стояли еще с вечера приготовленные Дуняшей зеркала.
cases.explain: «Наташином столе» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: — И я знаю, что она увидит; она и ___ видела.
cases.explain: «прошлого года» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: For about three minutes all were silent.
